failure_observed: The skill's audience model (modes A-E) was prose guidance with no checkable persona; comprehension was assessed by reviewer ratings, which Phase 5 showed can rise while reconstruction falls; nothing checked that abstracts or skim text preserve scope, intervals and denominators; and there was no protocol that turns 'did readers understand it?' into a measured, blinded, pre-registered result. Real Phase 9 drafts also show writers breaking their OWN term ledgers (e.g. BEIR v0.2.0 registers 'lexical baseline' as a forbidden synonym of BM25, then uses it 3 times).

components.summary: M02 reader knowledge model (schemas/reader_model.schema.json, templates/reader_model.json) + tools/audit_reader.py: unknown terms, term overload, prerequisite order, unaddressed misconceptions, unanswered reader questions; persona checks only with a reader model.
M11 density/terminology: excess precision vs own interval, synonym drift against the term ledger (research_story.md section 5 format), dense paragraphs.
M12 tools/skim_layer.py: build a verbatim, evidence-locked skim sheet; check compressed text for number/scope/hedge/uncertainty/denominator drift and generic headings.

M13 tools/comprehension_kit.py: hash-frozen pre-declared key, blinded visual-only vs full packets (HTML for humans, Markdown for LLM readers incl. drawn values), participant form, blind grading sheets, LLM proxy reader/grader tasks, scoring with bootstrap CIs and Krippendorff's alpha; templates/human_study_protocol.md.
V5 human review: tools/record_review.py; V5 passes only with a recorded review of the current render (stale after re-render).

change.summary: All Stage 3 code is in new files except two additive hooks. Stdlib only.

expected_improvement: Tool-level: writers get machine-checkable reader and compression feedback; comprehension becomes a measured, pre-registered, blinded outcome with inter-grader agreement instead of a rating. Reader-level: NOT claimed. The spec's Stage 3 acceptance requires blinded HUMAN reconstruction results; none have been collected. The LLM proxy run is a pipeline test and a cheap signal, not that evidence.
possible_regressions: Reader-model checks are only as good as the persona the author writes; a lazy persona (everything 'known') silences them.
Term, misconception and question matching is lexical (English); paraphrases can evade or trigger checks.
Excess-precision rule (one digit past the interval's leading digit) is a convention, not a law; some venues require fixed decimals.
LLM proxy readers see figures as text (drawn values), which is more precise than reading a bar length by eye.
Human studies need participants and time; without them Stage 3 acceptance stays pending, by design.
